questions.prompt: Does a parent have the right to withdraw a previously given "parental consent" for someone under 18 years of age with respect to an operator's license?
questions.explanation: A parent or guardian who signed consent for an applicant under 18 can withdraw it while that person is still under 18, unless they are self-supporting or married. The licence is then cancelled. Key words: "not self-supporting or married".

choices.text: Yes, providing the person is still under the age of 18 and is not self-supporting or married
Yes, provided that both parents verbally agree to withdraw the consent at a registry office
No, once it is given it remains in effect until the person reaches 18 years of age
No, but another consent form must be signed by both parents after a license suspension

questions.prompt: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, a driver will receive 2 demerits:
questions.explanation: Learner and probationary drivers may not carry more passengers than there are seat belts in the vehicle. Breaking this GDL condition costs 2 demerit points. Key words: "2 demerits", "seat belts".

choices.text: For having more passengers than there are seat belts
For not wearing a seat belt securely fastened
For not wearing a seat belt
For not wearing a seat belt properly adjusted

questions.prompt: Who is responsible and legally obligated to report any medical condition, change in health, or physical disability that may affect a driver's ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Drivers themselves are legally responsible for reporting any medical condition or disability that may affect their ability to drive safely. Key words: "legally obligated".

questions.prompt: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, a learner with a Class 7 operator's license is suspended when they accumulate:
questions.explanation: GDL drivers (learner and probationary) are suspended at 8 demerit points. Fully licensed drivers are suspended at 15. Key words: "a learner", "suspended".

questions.prompt: Under the Graduated Driver Licensing program, what is the minimum amount of time that a person must serve as a probationary Class 5 driver?
questions.explanation: A probationary (Class 5-GDL) driver must hold that licence for at least 2 years, and be suspension-free for the last 12 months, before they can become fully licensed. Key words: "probationary Class 5 driver".

questions.prompt: A road test will be refused by a driver examiner if:
questions.explanation: An examiner will refuse to conduct a road test in a vehicle that is not mechanically safe, for example one with faulty brakes, lights or signals.

choices.text: The vehicle has a seating capacity greater than 7
The vehicle is registered as a farm vehicle
The vehicle is a rental vehicle
The vehicle is not mechanically safe

questions.prompt: Alberta has a demerit point system where a fully licensed (non-learner, non-probationary) driver is suspended when they accumulate:
questions.explanation:
In Alberta, a fully licensed (non-learner, non-probationary Class 5) driver's license is automatically suspended if they accumulate 15 or more demerit points within a two-year period.
For drivers with a Graduated Driver's License (GDL), including those with a Class 7 learner's permit, the rules are stricter: their license is suspended if they accumulate 8 or more demerit points within a two-year period.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum age to apply for a Class 7 learner's licence in Alberta?
questions.explanation: You must be 14 or older to get a Class 7 learner's licence, with parental consent if you are under 18. (Driver's Guide p. 10)

questions.prompt: Who may supervise a Class 7 learner driver?
questions.explanation: A learner must be accompanied by a fully licensed (non-GDL) driver who is 18 or older and seated next to them. (Driver's Guide p. 10)

choices.text: A fully licensed (non-GDL) driver aged 18 or older, seated next to the learner
Any licensed driver aged 18 or older, seated anywhere in the vehicle
A probationary driver aged 21 or older

questions.prompt: During which hours is a Class 7 learner not permitted to drive?
questions.explanation: Learners may not drive from midnight to 5 a.m. This curfew applies to the learner stage only. (Driver's Guide p. 10)

questions.prompt: How long must you hold a Class 7 learner's licence before you can take the Class 5 road test?
questions.explanation: You must hold your learner's licence for at least one year. This time is extended if you receive a suspension. (Driver's Guide p. 10)

questions.prompt: What is the minimum age to hold a Class 5-GDL (probationary) licence?
questions.explanation: To become a probationary driver you must be at least 16, have held your learner's licence for a year, and pass the Class 5 road test. (Driver's Guide pp. 10, 13)

questions.prompt: Which of these is a condition for Class 5-GDL probationary drivers?
questions.explanation: Probationary drivers may not carry more passengers than there are seat belts. The midnight-to-5 a.m. curfew and the supervisor requirement apply to learners only. (Driver's Guide p. 10)

choices.text: No driving between midnight and 5 a.m.
A supervising driver must be in the front seat
No more passengers than there are seat belts

questions.prompt: Can a Class 5-GDL probationary driver act as the supervising driver for a learner?
questions.explanation: No. A probationary driver cannot supervise a learner. Only a fully licensed (non-GDL) driver aged 18 or older can. (Driver's Guide p. 10)

choices.text: Yes, if they are 18 or older
No, the supervisor must be fully licensed (non-GDL)
Yes, after one year as a probationary driver
Yes, if a parent gives written consent

questions.prompt: To exit the GDL program and receive a full Class 5 licence, you must:
questions.explanation: You must be at least 18, have been probationary for at least two years, and have no suspensions or traffic violations in the last 12 months. (Driver's Guide p. 11)

choices.text: Be at least 16 and have been probationary for 1 year
Pass a second knowledge test after 2 years
Be at least 18, have been probationary for 2 years, and have no suspensions or violations in the last 12 months
Be at least 21 and have no demerit points

questions.prompt: Completing an approved driver training course can reduce the probationary stage by up to:
questions.explanation: An approved driver training course, recorded on your licence as condition code U, can reduce the probationary stage by up to six months. (Driver's Guide p. 11)

questions.prompt: What blood alcohol level is allowed for a GDL driver (learner or probationary)?
questions.explanation: GDL drivers must have a zero alcohol and drug level when driving. (Driver's Guide pp. 10, 112)

questions.prompt: How many times per day may you take the knowledge test?
questions.explanation: There is a fee for each knowledge test, and you can take only one test per day. (Driver's Guide p. 11)

choices.text: As many times as you like

questions.prompt: Which of these results in an automatic failure on the Class 5 road test?
questions.explanation: Failing to stop completely before a stop sign, or before turning right on a red light, is an automatic fail regardless of your point total. (Driver's Guide p. 13)

choices.text: Using hand-over-hand steering on a turn
Parking successfully on the second attempt
Not stopping completely before turning right on a red light

questions.prompt: On the Class 5 road test, you fail automatically if you cannot park legally within how many attempts?
questions.explanation: Climbing the curb while parking, or being unable to park legally in three attempts, results in automatic failure. (Driver's Guide p. 13)

questions.prompt: When a peace officer asks, what documents must a driver produce?
questions.explanation: On request of a peace officer, a driver must produce their driver's licence, vehicle registration, and insurance. (Driver's Guide p. 15)

choices.text: Driver's licence, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance
Vehicle registration and a birth certificate
Proof of insurance and a vehicle inspection report

questions.prompt: The financial responsibility card that proves your vehicle is insured is commonly called the:
questions.explanation: Your insurance company issues a financial responsibility card, the pink card. It must be shown when registering a vehicle and when a peace officer asks. (Driver's Guide p. 20)

questions.prompt: A new Alberta resident moving from another Canadian province may use their out-of-province licence for how long?
questions.explanation: New residents from elsewhere in Canada may use their out-of-province licence for the first 90 days, and must apply for an Alberta licence within that time. (Driver's Guide p. 16)

questions.prompt: Your driver's licence has been stolen. What must you do?
questions.explanation: Report the theft to the police, then give a copy of the police report to the registry agent when you apply for a replacement. (Driver's Guide p. 19)

choices.text: Keep driving until your licence expires, then renew it
Wait 30 days in case it is returned
Report it to the police and apply for a replacement at a registry agent

questions.prompt: A fully licensed driver receives a warning letter about their demerit points at:
questions.explanation: Fully licensed drivers get a warning letter at 8 to 14 demerit points within two years, and are suspended at 15. (Driver's Guide p. 108)

questions.prompt: How long do demerit points stay on your driving record?
questions.explanation: Demerit points are removed two years after the date of the conviction. (Driver's Guide p. 110)

choices.text: 1 year from the date of conviction
5 years from the date of conviction
10 years from the date of conviction
2 years from the date of conviction

questions.prompt: How long is the first automatic suspension for reaching the demerit point limit?
questions.explanation: The first demerit suspension is one month, the second within a year is three months, and the third within two years is six months. (Driver's Guide p. 110)

questions.prompt: Completing a Government-approved defensive driving course before reaching 15 points gives you:
questions.explanation: A three-point credit is applied to your driving record for two years. (Driver's Guide p. 110)

choices.text: A 1-point credit on your driving record
A 3-point credit on your driving record

questions.prompt: How many demerit points are given for speeding 31 to 50 km/h over the limit?
questions.explanation: Speeding by 31 to 50 km/h over the limit costs 4 demerit points. Speeding by 51 km/h or more costs 6. (Driver's Guide p. 109)

questions.prompt: Which offence carries the most demerit points?
questions.explanation: Failing to remain at the scene of a collision carries 7 demerit points, the highest on the list. (Driver's Guide p. 109)

choices.text: Failing to stop for a school bus
Failing to remain at the scene of a collision
Failing to stop at a stop sign
